audits.text:
## 5bf6e2e7ed82

**Reproduced strict-scalar contract defect; audited source unchanged.** Generator
SHA-256: `11294de27243bfb10309eb543aac26639d0e44fae4cfaf35d041d1cc5b686a73`.
The audit `defect_lint` reports 111 accepted-invalid-scalar warnings across
`seed`, `sample_index`, and the four integer axes, plus one advisory
`object_count` structural-mismatch warning. The exact log is
`checks/audit/5bf6e2e7ed82-defect-lint/checks/5bf6e2e7ed82_audit_defect_lint.log`.

The independent source-bound reproducer at
`checks/audit/5bf6e2e7ed82/strict_scalar_reproducer.py` confirms three concrete
cases: `target_size=7.75` is silently coerced to observed size 7,
`sample_index=-1` is accepted, and `seed=True` is accepted. All three generated
grids pass `self_check`, which makes the invalid call indistinguishable from a
lawful sample downstream. The retained JSON includes the source/rule hashes,
call arguments, observed controls, shapes, and exact replay command. The task's
existing portable tests still pass 6/6, so they do not cover this contract.

A minimal repair would validate literal integer call arguments before
`schedule_profile`/`gen_ctx` and use `draw_int_strict` for integer axes. I did
not investigate the separate `object_count` warning deeply enough to classify
it as a defect; it remains an explicit diagnostic rather than a claim. No files
under the audited generator were modified.
